subject: general
question: National Education Day is observed on 11 November to celebrate the birthday of which Indian leader?
solution:
The correct answer is__** Maulana Abul Kalam Azad.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **National Education Day** is observed annually on **11 November** to commemorate the birthday of **Maulana Abul Kalam Azad**, an Indian scholar, freedom fighter, and the first Education Minister of independent India.
 
• Maulana Abul Kalam Azad played a key role in laying the foundation of India's education system and promoting universal education in the country.
 
• He was a strong advocate of primary education **for all children up to the age of 14, **regardless of caste, religion, or gender.
 
• Azad’s contributions led to the establishment of various educational institutions, including **the Indian Institutes of Technology (IITs) and the University Grants Commission (UGC).**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Role as Education Minister**: Maulana Abul Kalam Azad served as the first Education Minister of independent India from 1947 to 1958 and worked tirelessly to promote the importance of education in the country.
 
• **Educational Reforms**: Azad's tenure saw the establishment of prominent institutions such as the **Indian Institutes of Technology (IITs)**, **Indian Council for Cultural Relations (ICCR)**, and the **University Grants Commission (UGC)** to support higher education and cultural exchange.
 
• **Vision for Education**: Azad believed that education was the most powerful tool for social upliftment and national integration, and he strongly emphasized the need for scientific and technical education.
 
• **Legacy**: In recognition of his immense contribution to education, **11 November** was declared National Education Day by the Government of India in 2008 to highlight the importance of education and to honor Maulana Azad's vision for a progressive and educated nation.
